To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the IS and IVGMRs in the neutron-rich deformed nuclei around Zr isotopes have a double and quadruple peak structures, respectively, and that the threshold strength in the IV mode is generated by neutronic excitations only.
the GMR has two-peak structure due the mixing between the GMR and the GQR, and that the transition strength of the GMR increases with the neutron number.
the GQR and the GMR are strongly mixed, and the neutron excitation dominates the IVGMR and the threshold strength in neutron-rich nuclei.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a detailed study of the IS and the IV GMR in neutron-rich Zirconium isotopes.
the deformation effects on the GMR, particularly the mixing with the GQR, the effects of neutron excess, and the role of the neutron threshold strength.
the roles of deformation and neutron number on the GMR in neutron-rich Zirconium isotopes, and the effects of deformation on the mixing of the GMR and the GQR are found to be significant.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the neutron excess is the most important factor in the ISGMR in well-deformed nuclei.
the deformation effects are essential to describe the properties of the IS and the IV GMRs in well-deformed nuclei.

the neutron excess plays an important role on the ISGMR, while the deformation plays an important role both in the ISGQR and in the ISGMR.
